resolution: Fixed the fall-through on the --massive scale-lab map: the no-V8 loader's buildPhysicsColliders (world_loader.zig) had a flat MAX_RECTS=4096 collider cap and walked the instance buffer in order, so the ~28k building rects (which lead the buffer) filled the cap before the ground rows were reached — the player spawned on a ground slab whose collider had been clipped and fell through (at a triumphant 240fps, proving the one-big-mesh render path flies). Reworked the collider build into two passes: pass 0 registers WALKABLE FLOORS (sy <= step height), pass 1 registers SOLID WALLS, so the floor always wins the cap. The generator lays one world-spanning base slab as the first ground row, so it now always claims a collider slot and the player has solid ground under the entire map at any size; worst case at extreme scale is distant buildings going walk-through, never the floor. No-op for real bakes under 4096 instances. Pending the user's loader rebuild + playtest. Honest next step flagged: static whole-world collision should become spatial windowing (GTA-style near-player collider refresh) to make buildings solid at huge scale.
